reason: The hypothesis synthesizes findings from multiple distinct papers: it combines the observation of enhanced oxidation resistance and internal oxidation in ultrafine-grain HEAs (P2) with the atomistic mechanism of environment-induced FCC-to-BCC phase transformation (P5, P17, P19, P25, P31) and the phenomenon of oxide spallation and matrix segmentation in additively manufactured HEAs (P9, P14). It applies this combined mechanism to a new, specific alloy composition (Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3) with AM-induced defects, and proposes a controlled gas-environment test to isolate the role of oxidation in driving the phase transformation and failure, which none of the passages individually suggests.

non-uniform oxide scale growth at grain boundaries
spallation of oxide scale due to thermal stresses
FCC to BCC phase transformation induced by oxidation/corrosion
